title: SLO-aware staged holdpoints for multi-region Hosted API rollouts
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Our current Hosted API rollout workflows rely heavily on time-based pauses and manual checks during region and blue/green shifts. That has led to late detection of performance regressions during regional rollouts and rolling traffic shifts where downstream services or kernels degrade under load. Proposal: Add SLO-aware staged holdpoints into the deployment pipeline so the orchestrator automatically pauses traffic progression at defined checkpoints until SLOs are stable for a configurable observation window. Key behaviors: 1) Holdpoint triggers: p95 latency increase > X%, p99 latency > threshold, error-rate > Y requests/minute, token-cost spike, or custom customer-facing metric regressions. 2) Observation window: configurable (default 5m steady-state check + 15m extended). 3) Automated actions: if metrics pass, rollout resumes; if metrics breach abort thresholds, automatic rollback to last healthy variant and notify on-call; if metrics are borderline, escalate to manual approval with quick rollback button in Console. 4) Rollout policy DSL extension: add "holdpoint" objects with metric predicates, severity, and remediation actions. 5) Backward compatibility: default policies identical to current timeline-based behavior; teams can opt into SLO-driven gating. Implementation plan: - Extend traffic-controller service to support HOLD/PAUSE states and evaluate Prometheus/Grafana metrics via the existing telemetry bridge. - Add policy parser to Console and runtime config; expose policy editor in Console rollout workflows. - Implement fast rollback heuristics inside orchestrator (circuit-break + instant weight revert) and a safe drain path for existing connections. - Provide dashboards and alert rules: prebuilt Grafana panel and Slack/PagerDuty alerting templates. Acceptance criteria (must pass before rollout to production): - Unit + integration tests for rollout state machine and policy parser. - End-to-end QA: staged rollout in staging with synthetic traffic (50k RPS) demonstrating detection/resume/abort paths. - Two-week dogfood on internal services with canary policies enabled. - Docs and runbook updated (runbook link below). Artifacts and links: - Design doc (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/SLO-Aware+Holdpoints - Implementation PR (WIP): https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/7812 - Dashboards: https://grafana.redwood-infra.com/d/rollouts/slo-rollouts - Runbook: https://docs.redwood.ai/runbooks/rollout-holdpoints - Postmortem template for aborted rollouts: https://docs.redwood.ai/postmortems/rollout-abort-template Rollout plan: 1) Feature branch + unit tests (ENG sprint 10) 2) Canary in us-west on low-traffic tenant subset (non-customer-impact) 3) Enable SLO-holdpoints for internal teams and watch for 2 weeks 4) Gradual opt-in by customers via Console toggles 5) Full default enablement with telemetry-backed thresholds after 6 weeks Risks and trade-offs: - False positives (over-sensitive thresholds) could slow releases; mitigation: conservative defaults and a learn-and-tune phase. - Extra control-plane complexity; mitigation: reuse existing controller primitives and keep policy DSL minimal. - Cost of prolonged observation windows increases deployment time; mitigation: allow teams to opt for faster windows for low-risk releases.
